Closes #3266. An error is now thrown if a body validation schema is specified for `GET` or `HEAD` routes. The docs also explain now that the request body validation is only available for `POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTION` requests. The content-type parser documentation also now provides a more detailed explanation of when the request payload is parsed and when it is not.

#### Checklist

- [x] run `npm run test` and `npm run benchmark`
- [x] tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [x] documentation is changed or added
- [x] commit message and code follows the [Developer's Certification of Origin](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#developers-certificate-of-origin-11)
      and the [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issue_context.title: GET request payload validation error
comments:
I think the behavior we actually want is to throw/error if the definition of a GET route includes a schema for the incoming payload.


Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.
In case you or anybody else would like to take this work, target the next branch.

I take over this work. 
Or should we parse the payload of `GET` requests just like `DELETE` requests so that we treat `GET` and `DELETE` requests identically?
Definitely not. GET should not have bodies.
Alright, then I will throw an error if a GET route includes a schema 👍
You might want to do it for HEAD as well.

We should behave like what the [document](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/docs/Validation-and-Serialization.md#validation) said `validates the body of the request if it is a POST, PUT, or PATCH method.`.

If the method is not `POST, PUT or PATCH` and it specify a `body` schema. We can consider it as wrong usage and throw an error.

For `DELETE` and `OPTION`, maybe we need to update the document.

> Definitely not. GET should not have bodies.

Agreed.
Then we should change the documentation for `DELETE` and `OPTION` and throw an error for `GET` and `HEAD` if a schema is specified?
